item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":1,"rationale":"The covered agencies are mandatorily directed to publish proposed Common Rule revisions; the segment initiates and organizes rulemaking, while any binding legal consequence would arise only from later final rules.","evidence":"shall promptly jointly publish in the Federal Register the following proposed revisions to the Common Rule as it affects classified research"},{"segment_id":"2","code":1,"rationale":"HHS is assigned coordination responsibility and the agencies must issue specified proposals and solicit comment, but the segment does not itself enact the proposals or require their final adoption.","evidence":"The agencies shall jointly propose to prohibit waiver of informed consent for classified research."},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The OSTP Director must review an appeal but retains authority to choose whether the project is approved or disapproved, so no particular later legal outcome is dictated.","evidence":"The Director of OSTP shall review the IRB's decision and approve or disapprove the project"},{"segment_id":"4","code":4,"rationale":"The segment inseparably combines administrative determinations, reporting, and rulemaking duties with a presently operative prohibition on conducting covered research without personal agency-head approval.","evidence":"Agencies may not conduct any classified human research project subject to the Common Rule unless the agency head has personally approved the specific project."},{"segment_id":"5","code":1,"rationale":"The OSTP Director is assigned mandatory reporting and publication tasks, and the accompanying definitions clarify the memorandum's administration without independently changing substantive rights or status.","evidence":"The Director of OSTP shall report the total number of classified research projects and participating subjects to the President"},{"segment_id":"6","code":3,"rationale":"The memorandum itself prospectively imposes, beginning one year later, a substantive condition barring agencies from conducting or supporting classified human research unless they have promulgated the required rule.","evidence":"no agency shall conduct or support classified human research without having proposed and promulgated the Common Rule"}]}
